subject: Data retention exception request - FinPay
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Singh <a.singh@finpay.com>, John Miller <john.miller@finpay.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Data retention exception request - FinPay

Hi Aisha / John -

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side on the data-retention items you raised:

1) FinPay requirement: 0-retention for any PII in production inference payloads (requests/responses) for the payments workflow.
2) Logs: you still need basic billing/throughput metrics, but want those to be anonymized and retained only for a short window (30-90 days).
3) Audit: FinPay legal requested an exception to our standard 365-day operational logs for this scope; they asked for a proposed draft exception and any technical controls we can implement (filters, redaction, truncated KV cache).

Action items we discussed:
- Redwood: provide a proposed retention-exception draft, and confirm technical feasibility (what logs we need for billing, what can be avoided).
- FinPay: share any formal policy text or wording they need in the exception, and confirm whether PCI/TLS/other attestations will be required in addition.

Camila / Rafael - can you review the feasibility notes below and I'll follow up with a draft exception this afternoon?

Feasibility notes (high level):
- We can support a 'no-content' retention mode for customer routes where payloads are not stored at rest and are not logged (0 days).
- We retain minimal operational metrics (token counts, request timestamps) for billing and capacity planning; we can provide an anonymized export and shorten retention to 30-90 days for this account if needed.
- Some transient internal logs (traces, error dumps) may contain snippets in rare failure modes; we can configure stricter scrubbing and create an audit path where such dumps require a legal request to be accessed.

I'll attach a draft exception for initial review. Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up next week to walk the redlines and sign-off path.

Thanks -
Marissa
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0142

Attachment: retention-exception-draft.pdf

From: Aisha Singh <a.singh@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: John Miller <john.miller@finpay.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request - FinPay

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifying Qs from privacy/legal: 

1) When you say 'no-content' retention mode, does that apply to all environments (prod, staging) or only customer-controlled production routes? We need guarantees for production only; staging can retain logs for debugging under strict access controls.
2) For billing metrics: can you confirm exactly which attributes are retained (e.g., request timestamp, model id, token counts) and whether IP addresses or client identifiers are included in those metrics? We'd like to avoid any persistent mapping back to a user identifier.
3) For the transient internal logs you mention - can Redwood commit to a process where any retrieval of those logs for FinPay-specific incidents requires a signed legal request (and is logged in your audit trail)?

I've looped John (ops) for technical confirmation on what FinPay needs in the exception text. Once we have your draft, our legal will mark up and return redlines.

Aisha Singh
Senior Privacy Counsel, FinPay
a.singh@finpay.com

On Apr 22, 2028, at 2:05 PM, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message above)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Singh <a.singh@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request - FinPay

Hi Aisha -

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers below, plus what I'll propose in the draft.

1) Scope: we can support 0-retention for production inference routes only. Staging and test environments will remain on standard retention but we can restrict access to a small set of engineers with MFA. I will add explicit environment scoping language to the exception.

2) Billing/metrics: in the shortened-retention mode we retain: timestamp, model identifier (model-v1), token count, request latency. We do NOT persist raw request/response content, user identifiers, or IP addresses in the anonymized export. We can hash any client_id with a salted, truncated hash if you need deduping without re-identification.

3) Internal log access: yes - any time an internal engineer requests a FinPay-specific internal trace that may contain payload snippets, they must file a legal incident request. We can log that access and include an immutable audit entry. I'll add that language and propose a 3-party access matrix in the draft (Redwood security, Redwood legal, FinPay legal).

Technical constraints/notes:
- The KV cache cannot be fully disabled for some models without a performance impact; however we can truncate KV retention immediately after request completion and ensure no long-lived cache entries are persisted to disk.
- For billing we still need token counts to compute usage charges. If FinPay prefers, we can provide periodic aggregated billing exports instead of per-request metrics.

I'm attaching a short implementation note and will fold the language into Marissa's exception draft: retention-exception-draft.pdf

- Camila
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachment: retention-exception-draft.pdf

Camila - this looks promising. Couple follow-ups from ops: 

- Can you confirm the shortened metric retention window options (30 / 60 / 90 days)? FinPay prefers 30 if feasible.
- For aggregated billing exports - can you provide a sample CSV format and cadence (daily/weekly)? We'd prefer weekly aggregated totals at first.

If the technical side is straightforward we're happy to proceed to legal redlines. I'll ask our procurement team to prepare language about SLA credits tied to any data-handling deviations.

John Miller
Head of Platform Ops, FinPay
john.miller@finpay.com
